summary.name: Brave
summary.one_liner: Brave is a privacy-focused, Chromium-based web browser that blocks ads, trackers and cookie pop-ups by default, with optional paid VPN and related services.
use_cases: Blocking ads and trackers while browsing
Speeding up page loads and saving mobile data
Switching from Chrome or Firefox to a more private browser
Using a private search engine instead of Google
Encrypting all device traffic with a paid VPN
summary.what_it_does: Brave is a web browser that blocks third-party ads, trackers, fingerprinting and cookie consent pop-ups by default, which the page says reduces data, battery and CPU use and makes websites load faster. It upgrades pages to HTTPS where possible and includes Global Privacy Control enabled by default. It is built on the open-source Chromium core, and its own client code is under the Mozilla Public License 2.0. Related offerings include Brave Search, a private search engine, Brave Firewall + VPN (a subscription covering up to 5 devices), Brave Rewards (optional ads that pay BAT tokens), and Brave Wallet. Brave Origin is a paid, one-time-purchase ($59.99 US) lighter version of the browser with some features removed.
notable: Ad, tracker and cookie pop-up blocking on by default, including YouTube ads
Built on open-source Chromium; client code under MPL 2.0
Brave Search private search engine with its own index
Optional BAT rewards and Brave Wallet
caveats: VPN, Brave Talk Premium and Brave Origin are paid subscriptions or purchases
Brave Origin costs $59.99 US one-time and removes features like Leo, News, Rewards, VPN and Wallet
Speed claims (3x faster than Chrome, 3x-6x faster pages) are the vendor's own claims
